tiers.label: Tier 1 – Universal
tiers.definition: High-quality teaching and supports routinely available to all students.

tiers.label: Tier 2 – Targeted
tiers.definition: Additional, planned support for an identified functional need, skill or goal. Tier 1 continues.

tiers.label: Tier 3 – Intensive
tiers.definition: Highly individualised, sustained and coordinated support. Tier 1 continues.

activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands
Responding to the Feelings of Others

levelinfo.rule: Universal environment of support. No diagnosis or referral is required. This does not by itself indicate individualised intervention.
levelinfo.intensity: Ordinary supports/resources available in the setting

levelinfo.rule: Usual responsive classroom teaching. Tier 1 continues for every student.
levelinfo.intensity: Brief, occasional; within usual classroom practice

levelinfo.rule: Usually Tier 2 when additional planned support is provided for an identified need. Confirm the tier from coordination, breadth, settings, risk and review requirements.
levelinfo.intensity: Regular, planned and personalised; at specific times/settings

levelinfo.rule: May sit at Tier 2 or Tier 3. Determine the school tier from breadth, complexity, settings, risk, staff involved and review frequency rather than from Profile level alone.
levelinfo.intensity: Frequent, personalised; on most days/relevant settings

levelinfo.rule: Usually Tier 3 because support is sustained and highly individualised. Confirm using the coordination response and duty-of-care requirements.
levelinfo.intensity: Sustained, highly individualised; consistently across activity/settings

roles.label: Classroom Teacher
roles.hint: The subject or classroom teacher who teaches the student.

roles.label: Education Support Staff
roles.hint: Staff who provide agreed in-class or personal assistance under teacher and plan direction. Most schools have one name for this — pick or type yours.

roles.label: Disability Inclusion Leader
roles.hint: Coordinates plans, meetings, evidence and funding processes.

roles.label: Inclusion Leader
roles.hint: Whole-school inclusive practice, systems and professional learning.

roles.label: Wellbeing Lead
roles.hint: Wellbeing coordination, check-ins, re-engagement, safe spaces.

roles.label: Mental Health Practitioner
roles.hint: In-school counselling, psychology or mental health support.

roles.label: Principal Class
roles.hint: Principal, assistant principal or equivalent leadership.

roles.label: Year Level Leader
roles.hint: Year level, house or sub-school leadership.

roles.label: Literacy Lead
roles.hint: Literacy teaching, data and intervention across the school.

roles.label: Numeracy Lead
roles.hint: Numeracy teaching, data and intervention across the school.

roles.label: Behaviour Lead
roles.hint: Behaviour support planning, coaching and incident review.

roles.label: Personal and Social Capabilities Lead
roles.hint: Explicit teaching of self-management and social skills.

roles.label: Cultural Lead
roles.hint: Cultural safety, community connection and family partnership.

roles.label: Daily Organiser
roles.hint: Relief staffing, cover and timetable changes on the day.

roles.label: Support Coordinator
roles.hint: Coordinates ES staff on the day, triages DI and student needs and handles DI admin.

roles.label: School Nurse
roles.hint: Health support plans, medication and health procedures.

roles.label: First Aid Officer
roles.hint: Day-to-day first aid response and health records.

roles.label: Allied Health Professional
roles.hint: Speech, OT, physio or psychology — internal or external.

roles.label: Transition Coordinator
roles.hint: Transition in, between years, and to post-school pathways.

roleSupports.action: Give school-implementable recommendations
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should give the school recommendations for {preferredName} that can be implemented in an ordinary classroom by ordinary staff, naming who does what and how often, and review them with the school at least annually with family consent, so advice is usable rather than aspirational.
roleSupports.frequency: at each report and reviewed at least annually
roleSupports.intensity: Written recommendations with named roles and frequencies
evidence: recommendations that could not be implemented and why

roleSupports.action: Observe in the real setting before advising
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should observe {preferredName} in the actual classroom or setting before finalising recommendations, and adjust them to what the environment allows, so the advice fits the school {preferredName} attends.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once before each set of recommendations
roleSupports.intensity: In-setting observation followed by revised written advice
evidence: what the observation changed in the advice

roleSupports.action: Train and monitor the staff implementing the technique
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should train the school staff who implement any prescribed technique, program or equipment for {preferredName}, observe them doing it, and review it at an agreed interval, so the technique is delivered as intended and safely.
roleSupports.frequency: initial training, observation within the first month, then reviewed each semester
roleSupports.intensity: Hands-on training with observation and sign-off

roleSupports.action: Co-write the behaviour support plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should write {preferredName}'s behaviour support plan with {preferredName}, the family and the teaching team, naming the triggers, the early signs, the agreed response and who does what, so every adult responds the same way rather than to their own judgement in the moment.
roleSupports.frequency: written once and reviewed each term or after any significant incident
roleSupports.intensity: Documented plan with named responders, known to everyone who teaches the student
evidence: how closely the agreed response was followed

roleSupports.action: Coach staff in the agreed response
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should coach {preferredName}'s teachers in the agreed response and de-escalation approach, observe it in practice and give feedback, so the plan is used as written rather than as each adult remembers it.
roleSupports.frequency: initial coaching, then observation and feedback once a term
roleSupports.intensity: Modelling, observation and feedback with the staff involved

roleSupports.action: Review the incident pattern, not just the incident
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should review {preferredName}'s incident records at least fortnightly, looking for patterns of time, subject, setting or person, and change the plan where a pattern is clear, so the response addresses the cause rather than repeating the consequence.
roleSupports.frequency: at least fortnightly
roleSupports.intensity: Pattern analysis with documented changes to the plan

roleSupports.action: Check consequences against the plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should check any consequence, suspension or referral proposed for {preferredName} against the plan and the identified disability-related need before it is applied, so a response to disability-related behaviour is not treated as a simple choice.
roleSupports.frequency: before any consequence or referral is applied
roleSupports.intensity: Plan checked and the decision recorded with its reasoning
evidence: consequences applied and their consistency with the plan

roleSupports.action: Raise implementation barriers rather than dropping the adjustment
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should raise with the plan coordinator any adjustment for {preferredName} that cannot be implemented as written, within a fortnight of the problem appearing, so it is redesigned rather than quietly dropped.
roleSupports.frequency: within a fortnight of any implementation problem
roleSupports.intensity: Direct written or verbal notification with the specific barrier named
evidence: barriers raised and what was agreed instead

roleSupports.action: Bring specific evidence to the review
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should bring specific evidence to each review of {preferredName}'s plan — what was tried, what happened, work samples and the level of support needed — rather than a general impression, so decisions rest on classroom reality.
roleSupports.frequency: before each review meeting
roleSupports.intensity: Short written evidence per adjustment, with work samples where relevant

roleSupports.action: Brief the relief teacher before a planned absence
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should leave the class summary of {preferredName}'s adjustments for any relief teacher before a planned absence, including what to do if things are difficult, so a day with a different teacher is not a day without adjustments.
roleSupports.frequency: before every planned absence
roleSupports.intensity: Written summary left with the lesson plan
evidence: days with relief staff and how they went

roleSupports.action: Keep teaching and quality first teaching in place
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should continue to teach, assess and plan for {preferredName} alongside any targeted or intensive support, keeping responsibility for {preferredName}'s learning rather than transferring it to the support staff working with them.
roleSupports.frequency: every lesson
roleSupports.intensity: Teacher-led planning, teaching and assessment continues at every level of support
evidence: teacher-set goals and progress against them
who directs the support in the room

roleSupports.action: Make sure identity is part of the plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s cultural identity, language and community connections are reflected in the plan, with the family's consent about what is recorded, so support is built on who {preferredName} is rather than only on what is difficult.
roleSupports.frequency: at each plan review
roleSupports.intensity: Family-led contribution recorded in the plan with consent
evidence: what the family and student identify as important
actLabels: Responding to the Feelings of Others

roleSupports.action: Make meetings work for the family
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should arrange {preferredName}'s meetings so the family can take part — timing, location, interpreters, who attends and how the meeting is run — and check with the family afterwards that it worked, so participation is real rather than formal.
roleSupports.frequency: before and after each meeting
roleSupports.intensity: Arrangements agreed with the family in advance and checked afterwards
evidence: what the family asks to change

roleSupports.action: Brief staff on culturally responsive practice
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should brief the staff working with {preferredName} on the culturally responsive practice agreed with the family, including what to avoid, before those staff first work with {preferredName}, so cultural safety does not depend on individual awareness.
roleSupports.frequency: before first contact and at the start of each year
roleSupports.intensity: Briefing with the agreed practice written down
evidence: staff practice reported by the student and family

roleSupports.action: Connect the student with community and mentoring
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should connect {preferredName} with cultural mentoring or community programs the family agrees to, and follow up that the connection was made, so the school is not the only source of support.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once a semester, with follow-up within a month
roleSupports.intensity: Referral plus follow-up confirming contact

roleSupports.action: Keep cover consistent for this student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should keep cover for {preferredName}'s classes as consistent as possible, using the same relief teachers where there is a choice, so an absent teacher does not also mean an unfamiliar adult every time.
roleSupports.frequency: each time a class is covered
roleSupports.intensity: Same relief staff used where a choice exists
evidence: how often a familiar adult covered the class

roleSupports.action: Get the summary to the relief teacher
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure the relief teacher receives {preferredName}'s one-page summary of adjustments before the lesson starts, so a covered lesson is not a lesson without adjustments.
roleSupports.frequency: before every covered lesson
roleSupports.intensity: Summary supplied with the cover notes as a matter of routine
evidence: covered lessons where the summary was supplied

roleSupports.action: Protect timetabled support staffing
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should keep {preferredName}'s timetabled support staffing in place rather than redeploying it to cover elsewhere, and tell the plan owner the same day when it genuinely cannot be held, so the loss is visible rather than silent.
roleSupports.frequency: each day support is timetabled
roleSupports.intensity: Allocation protected, with same-day notification when it cannot be
evidence: days the agreed support was not available and why

roleSupports.action: Convene and document the student support group
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should convene and document a student support group meeting for {preferredName} each term, recording the agreed adjustments, who is responsible for each one and the review date, and sharing that record with every teacher who teaches {preferredName}, so the same adjustments are implemented across every class rather than in some of them.
roleSupports.frequency: once each term, and after any significant change
roleSupports.intensity: Planned meeting with documented actions and named owners
evidence: adjustments agreed and who owns each one

roleSupports.action: Keep the record of adjustments current
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should keep {preferredName}'s record of adjustments current, updating it whenever an adjustment is added, changed or faded, and checking the written record against what is actually happening in classes at least once a term, so the documented plan and {preferredName}'s daily experience describe the same thing.
roleSupports.frequency: updated as changes occur, checked against practice each term
roleSupports.intensity: Record maintained by one named person, cross-checked with teachers
evidence: date and reason for each change
gaps found between the record and practice

roleSupports.action: Brief new and relieving staff before they teach the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should brief every new teacher, casual relief teacher and support staff member before they work with {preferredName}, using a one-page summary of the agreed adjustments and what to do if things go wrong, so support does not drop away when staffing changes.
roleSupports.frequency: before the first lesson with any new or relieving staff member
roleSupports.intensity: Short verbal briefing plus a written one-page summary
evidence: whether adjustments continued during the staffing change

roleSupports.action: Gather evidence across the year, not the week before
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should collect evidence for {preferredName}'s plan and any funding or profile process across the whole year — teacher observations, work samples, specialist reports, student voice and family voice — rather than in the fortnight beforehand, so the picture presented is an accurate description of a normal school week.
roleSupports.frequency: ongoing, with a collection point each term
roleSupports.intensity: Structured collection against each functional area, held in one place
evidence: range and dates of evidence held

roleSupports.action: Review each term what can be faded
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should review with {preferredName}'s teachers each term which adjustments are still needed, which should increase and which can be faded, so the level of adult support matches current evidence rather than what was agreed a year ago.
roleSupports.frequency: once each term
roleSupports.intensity: Structured review of each adjustment against recent evidence
evidence: adjustments faded and what happened next

roleSupports.action: Timetable the agreed support before the term starts
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should arrange and timetable the agreed additional support for {preferredName} — staffing, spaces and equipment — before the term begins and confirm it with each teacher, so the adjustment is available from the first lesson instead of being negotiated week by week.
roleSupports.frequency: before the start of each term and after any timetable change
roleSupports.intensity: Confirmed allocation in writing before the term starts
evidence: lessons where the agreed support was not available and why

roleSupports.action: Escalate unresolved implementation barriers
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should escalate to the principal class any barrier that stops an agreed adjustment being implemented for {preferredName} and that has not been resolved within a fortnight of being raised, so problems are dealt with at the level that can actually fix them.
roleSupports.frequency: whenever a barrier remains unresolved after a fortnight
roleSupports.intensity: Written escalation naming the barrier and what is needed

roleSupports.action: Translate specialist advice into school actions
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should meet with the specialists involved with {preferredName}, with family consent, and translate their recommendations into specific school actions with a named owner and a start date, so advice becomes practice rather than a report in a file.
roleSupports.frequency: after each new report and at least once a year
roleSupports.intensity: Documented conversion of each recommendation into an owned action
evidence: recommendations received and the action taken for each

roleSupports.action: Keep the agreed response available
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s agreed first aid response, medication and equipment are available and in date at all times the school operates, including sport and offsite activities, so the response does not depend on where {preferredName} is that day.
roleSupports.frequency: checked at the start of each term and before each offsite activity
roleSupports.intensity: Stock, currency and location checked against the plan
evidence: occasions the response was needed and what was available

roleSupports.action: Record and pass on every event
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should record every first aid event involving {preferredName} and pass it to the health plan owner and the family the same day, so a pattern is noticed early rather than at the end of term.
roleSupports.frequency: same day, every time
roleSupports.intensity: Written record shared with the plan owner and family

roleSupports.action: Brief the staff on duty
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should brief the staff on yard and sport duty on {preferredName}'s signs and the required response, at the start of each term and whenever the duty roster changes, so the right response is available wherever {preferredName} is.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each term and on roster changes
roleSupports.intensity: Briefing plus a response card carried by duty staff

roleSupports.action: Put the universal practices in place first
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure the practices that reduce the need for individual adjustment — predictable routines, accessible materials, clear instructions, known expectations — are in place across the school, so individual adjustments are reserved for what universal practice cannot cover.
roleSupports.frequency: reviewed each semester as part of school planning
roleSupports.intensity: Whole-school practice, monitored and supported rather than assumed
evidence: individual adjustments no longer needed once universal practice improved

roleSupports.action: Look at patterns across students, not just this one
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should look for patterns across the students on plans — the same barrier appearing in the same subject, setting or time of day — and report them to leadership each semester, so recurring problems are fixed once rather than student by student.
roleSupports.frequency: each semester
roleSupports.intensity: Cross-cohort analysis with a written report to leadership
evidence: patterns identified and the whole-school change made

roleSupports.action: Run professional learning on the adjustments in use
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should run professional learning for staff on the adjustments actually in use in the school, with practice and follow-up rather than a single session, so staff can implement them confidently.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once a semester with follow-up in teams
roleSupports.intensity: Sessions with modelling, practice and follow-up support

roleSupports.action: Build the literacy adjustment into unit planning
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should work with {preferredName}'s teachers at the start of each unit to build the agreed literacy adjustment into the unit's texts, tasks and assessments, so the adjustment is part of the planned work rather than something added when {preferredName} struggles.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each unit
roleSupports.intensity: Planning conversation per unit with the adjustment written into the plan
evidence: student access to the unit's texts

roleSupports.action: Set the reading demand of materials
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should check the reading demand of the materials {preferredName} is given and supply an accessible version at the agreed reading level, keeping the same learning goal, so reading load is not the reason {preferredName} cannot show what they know.
roleSupports.frequency: for each unit and before each assessment
roleSupports.intensity: Materials checked and adapted in advance, learning goal unchanged

roleSupports.action: Model the literacy strategy in class
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should model the agreed explicit literacy strategy in {preferredName}'s classes and coach the teacher to continue it, so the strategy is used consistently rather than only when a specialist is present.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once per teacher, then follow-up coaching each term
roleSupports.intensity: In-class modelling followed by teacher-led practice and feedback

roleSupports.action: Coordinate targeted literacy intervention
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should coordinate a targeted literacy intervention for {preferredName} at an agreed frequency, with an entry point set from assessment data and progress checked at a set interval, so the intervention is adjusted on evidence rather than continued out of habit.
roleSupports.frequency: sessions at the agreed frequency, progress checked every five weeks
roleSupports.intensity: Small-group or individual instruction with documented entry point and progress checks
evidence: transfer of the skill into class work

roleSupports.action: Short-term goal-focused individual sessions
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should provide short-term, goal-focused individual sessions with {preferredName} at an agreed frequency, with the goals and a review point written down at the start, so support is purposeful and its effect can be judged.
roleSupports.frequency: an agreed number of sessions, commonly weekly, with a review point
roleSupports.intensity: Individual sessions with documented goals and a planned end or review
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Turn session work into classroom strategies
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should give {preferredName}'s teachers two or three specific, practical classroom strategies drawn from the sessions, with {preferredName}'s consent about what is shared, so the same approach is used in class and in the session.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of the support and after each review point
roleSupports.intensity: Brief written strategies plus a conversation with the teaching team
evidence: strategies used in class and their effect
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Contribute to the safety or support plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should contribute to {preferredName}'s safety or support plan where a risk has been identified, setting out the warning signs, the agreed response and who does what, and review it after any incident, so staff respond consistently rather than improvising.
roleSupports.frequency: at plan development, then reviewed each term and after any incident
roleSupports.intensity: Documented plan with named responders and review points
evidence: how closely the agreed response was followed
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Warm handover to an external service
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make a warm handover to any external service {preferredName} is referred to, with family consent, and follow up within a fortnight to confirm contact was made, so a referral does not end at the point of paperwork.
roleSupports.frequency: at referral, with follow-up within a fortnight
roleSupports.intensity: Direct contact between practitioners plus follow-up confirmation
evidence: referrals made and whether contact was established
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Coach staff in the agreed regulation approach
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should coach the staff who work with {preferredName} in the agreed co-regulation and de-escalation approach, modelling it and observing it in practice, so the approach is used the same way by everyone rather than differently in each class.
roleSupports.frequency: initial coaching, then observation and feedback once a term
roleSupports.intensity: Modelling, observation and feedback with the staff involved
evidence: consistency of the response across staff
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Build the numeracy adjustment into unit planning
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should work with {preferredName}'s mathematics teachers at the start of each unit to build the agreed numeracy adjustment into the tasks and assessments, so access is planned rather than improvised in the lesson.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each unit
roleSupports.intensity: Planning conversation per unit with the adjustment written into the plan

roleSupports.action: Provide the agreed tools and scaffolds
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName} has the agreed numeracy tools and scaffolds — concrete materials, a calculator, formula or steps reference — available in every relevant lesson, so working memory and recall are not what limits the mathematics {preferredName} can do.
roleSupports.frequency: in every relevant lesson
roleSupports.intensity: Tools available by default, without the student having to ask
evidence: tools used and by whose prompt

roleSupports.action: Set the entry point from data
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should use {preferredName}'s numeracy assessment data to set the point the teaching starts from, and share that with the teachers, so tasks sit where {preferredName} can actually work rather than at the year level by default.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each year and after each assessment cycle
roleSupports.intensity: Data analysis translated into a stated entry point per teacher
evidence: match between tasks set and the entry point

roleSupports.action: Coordinate targeted numeracy intervention
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should coordinate a targeted numeracy intervention for {preferredName} at an agreed frequency, checking progress at a set interval and stopping or changing it if the evidence does not show growth, so time out of class is justified by what it produces.
roleSupports.frequency: sessions at the agreed frequency, progress checked every five weeks
roleSupports.intensity: Small-group or individual instruction with documented progress checks

roleSupports.action: Maintain and review the health support plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should maintain {preferredName}'s health support plan with the family and the treating practitioner, train the staff named in it, and review it at least annually and after any health event, so the school response is current and delivered by trained people.
roleSupports.frequency: reviewed annually and after any health event
roleSupports.intensity: Written plan, named trained staff, training currency tracked
evidence: health events and the response given

roleSupports.action: Make sure the health procedure travels with the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s medication, equipment and health procedure are available wherever the school program takes place, including excursions, camps and sport, so participation is never limited by where the equipment is kept.
roleSupports.frequency: before every offsite activity and daily on site
roleSupports.intensity: Checked against the plan before each activity
evidence: occasions the procedure was needed offsite

roleSupports.action: Brief staff on signs and the required response
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should brief the staff who teach or supervise {preferredName} on the signs to watch for and the exact response required, before those staff first work with {preferredName} and again each year, so the response does not depend on who happens to be there.
roleSupports.frequency: before first contact and annually
roleSupports.intensity: Briefing plus a written response card held where staff can reach it

roleSupports.action: Review after any health incident
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should review the plan with the family after any health incident involving {preferredName}, within a week, and change the plan where the incident showed it was needed, so the plan improves each time it is tested.
roleSupports.frequency: within a week of any health incident
roleSupports.intensity: Documented review with the family and changes made to the plan
evidence: incidents and the plan changes that followed

roleSupports.action: Resource the agreed adjustments
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure the adjustments agreed for {preferredName} are resourced — staffing, time, spaces and equipment — and named in the school's planning, so implementation does not depend on the goodwill of individual staff.
roleSupports.frequency: at each planning and budget cycle, and when needs change
roleSupports.intensity: Allocation confirmed in the school's own planning documents
evidence: adjustments that could not be delivered for resourcing reasons

roleSupports.action: Approve and time-limit any reduction in access
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should approve, document and review any arrangement that reduces {preferredName}'s access to the full timetable or program, setting a review date and a written plan for returning to full access, so a short-term measure does not quietly become permanent.
roleSupports.frequency: at the point of the decision, then reviewed at least every four weeks
roleSupports.intensity: Written approval, named review date, plan to restore full access

roleSupports.action: Meet the family at leadership level
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should meet {preferredName}'s family at agreed points across the year, and whenever the family raises an unresolved concern, so concerns are heard by someone who can act on them and the relationship does not rest on one staff member.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once a semester and whenever a concern is unresolved
roleSupports.intensity: Direct leadership contact with agreed follow-up actions
evidence: concerns raised and how each was resolved

roleSupports.action: Approve and review safety-critical arrangements
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should approve the risk assessment and duty-of-care arrangements for any safety-critical adjustment for {preferredName}, confirm the staff involved are trained, and review the arrangement after any incident, so safety does not depend on informal practice.
roleSupports.frequency: before the arrangement starts, then reviewed each term and after any incident
roleSupports.intensity: Documented approval, named trained staff, incident review

roleSupports.action: Build the adjustments into staff professional learning
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should include the practices {preferredName} depends on in whole-staff professional learning and planning, so the adjustment is part of how the school teaches rather than an exception a few staff know about.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once a year in the professional learning schedule
roleSupports.intensity: Scheduled whole-staff learning with follow-up in teams
evidence: staff confidence and consistency reported by teachers

roleSupports.action: Protect the plan through staffing and year-level changes
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s plan and adjustments are handed over whenever the teaching team, year level or leadership changes, with the handover completed before the change takes effect, so nothing has to be rebuilt from scratch.
roleSupports.frequency: before every staffing, year level or leadership change
roleSupports.intensity: Documented handover with the receiving staff named

roleSupports.action: Teach the specific skill explicitly
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should teach {preferredName} the specific self-management or social skill named in the plan explicitly, at an agreed time each week, and tell the teachers which skill to reinforce that fortnight, so the skill is taught rather than expected.
roleSupports.frequency: one session a week, with the reinforcement focus shared each fortnight
roleSupports.intensity: Explicit teaching with a named focus reinforced in class
evidence: the skill in use outside the session
student's own account of what is getting easier

roleSupports.action: Put the capability goal in the curriculum plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s personal and social capability goal appears in the curriculum plan and in reporting alongside academic goals, so growth in these areas is recognised as learning rather than as behaviour.
roleSupports.frequency: at each planning and reporting cycle
roleSupports.intensity: Goal written into planning and reported on
evidence: progress reported against the capability goal

roleSupports.action: Set up a structured social opportunity
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should set up a structured activity at break times that {preferredName} can join with a known adult nearby, and step that adult back as {preferredName} settles, so social contact is available without depending on an adult being present.
roleSupports.frequency: at the agreed break times each week
roleSupports.intensity: Structured activity with adult support that reduces over time

roleSupports.action: Co-design the regulation strategies with the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should design {preferredName}'s self-regulation strategies with {preferredName} rather than for them, write them in {preferredName}'s words and share them with staff with consent, so the strategies are ones {preferredName} will actually use.
roleSupports.frequency: designed once and reviewed each term with the student
roleSupports.intensity: Student-led design with adult scribing, shared with consent
evidence: strategies the student chooses to use
what the student asks to change
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Provide the agreed assistance, prompting before helping
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should provide the agreed in-class assistance to {preferredName} under teacher and plan direction, prompting the agreed strategy before giving direct help, and recording how much prompting was needed, so support can be faded on evidence rather than habit.
roleSupports.frequency: in each lesson where the agreed adjustment applies
roleSupports.intensity: Prompt first, direct assistance only where the prompt is not enough
evidence: tasks completed with less help than last time

roleSupports.action: Prepare adapted materials before the lesson
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should prepare or adapt {preferredName}'s materials in the agreed format before the lesson begins, under teacher direction, so {preferredName} starts the task at the same time as everyone else.
roleSupports.frequency: before each lesson where adapted materials are needed
roleSupports.intensity: Materials ready in advance to the agreed specification
evidence: lessons started on time with the right materials

roleSupports.action: Support unstructured times
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should be available to {preferredName} at the agreed unstructured times — recess, lunch or transitions — supporting entry into an activity or group rather than supervising from beside them, so the time is used well without creating dependence on an adult.
roleSupports.frequency: at the agreed break or transition times each day
roleSupports.intensity: Available nearby, actively supporting entry to an activity, stepping back once settled

roleSupports.action: Record observations against the plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should record short, specific observations of {preferredName} against the goals in the plan each week and give them to the teacher and the plan coordinator, so decisions are made on what is actually happening in lessons.
roleSupports.frequency: weekly
roleSupports.intensity: Brief written observations tied to the plan goals

roleSupports.action: Support the personal care or health routine
roleSupports.wording: The {role}, where trained and named in the plan, should support {preferredName}'s agreed personal care or health routine at the times set out in the plan, in a private space and in a way that maintains dignity and builds whatever independence is possible, so the routine is met safely without drawing attention.
roleSupports.frequency: at the times set out in the plan
roleSupports.intensity: Trained staff only, following the documented procedure, privacy maintained
evidence: steps the student now manages independently

roleSupports.action: Support excursions, camps and offsite activities
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should support {preferredName} on excursions, camps and offsite activities according to the risk assessment completed before the activity, so {preferredName} takes part in the same program as everyone else.
roleSupports.frequency: for each offsite activity
roleSupports.intensity: Support level set by the risk assessment for that activity
evidence: supports that were needed on the day

roleSupports.action: Translate the plan into subject-level adjustments
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should work with each subject teacher at the start of every unit to turn {preferredName}'s plan into the specific adjustments that unit needs, so the plan is applied to the actual work rather than sitting above it.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each unit in each subject
roleSupports.intensity: Short planning conversation per subject with agreed unit-level adjustments
evidence: student access to the unit's tasks

roleSupports.action: Model the adjustment in the classroom
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should model or co-teach the agreed adjustment in {preferredName}'s classes at least once per teacher, then hand it back to the teacher, so staff see how it works rather than only reading about it.
roleSupports.frequency: at least once per teacher, and after any new adjustment is agreed
roleSupports.intensity: In-class modelling followed by teacher-led practice
evidence: teacher confidence and use after modelling

roleSupports.action: Check adjustments are visible in practice
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should check each term whether {preferredName}'s agreed adjustments are visible in classroom practice, and feed what is found back to the teacher and the plan coordinator without blame, so gaps are found by the school rather than by the family.
roleSupports.frequency: once a term across a sample of classes
roleSupports.intensity: Short classroom visits against a specific list of agreed adjustments
evidence: gaps and what was done about them

roleSupports.action: Arrange assessment adjustments in advance
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should arrange {preferredName}'s agreed assessment adjustments — such as extra time, an alternative format, a separate space or a reader or scribe — before each formal assessment, checking each one against what the task is meant to assess, so access is provided without changing what is being measured.
roleSupports.frequency: before each formal assessment
roleSupports.intensity: Arranged in advance and confirmed with the student and the teacher
evidence: student report of the assessment conditions

roleSupports.action: Preview the week with the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should meet {preferredName} at the start of each week to preview what is coming — assessments, changes to routine, unfamiliar activities — and note anything that needs preparing, so the week holds fewer surprises.
roleSupports.frequency: once at the start of each week
roleSupports.intensity: Short individual meeting with a written or visual summary of the week
evidence: what the student flagged as difficult
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Start and end of day check-in
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should check in with {preferredName} at the start and end of each day to set up equipment, materials and the day's plan and to close the day off, so the day starts organised and does not end on an unresolved problem.
roleSupports.frequency: twice a day, every day
roleSupports.intensity: Brief, predictable individual contact at fixed times
evidence: issues resolved before the student goes home

roleSupports.action: Be present at the identified hard transitions
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should be present at the transitions {preferredName} finds hardest, prompting the agreed strategy before offering direct help, and stepping back as {preferredName} manages the transition independently, so support fades as skill grows.
roleSupports.frequency: at the identified transitions each day they occur
roleSupports.intensity: Present nearby, prompting first, direct help only if the prompt is not enough
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Watch attendance and engagement patterns
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should track {preferredName}'s attendance and engagement each week, act on a pattern in the week it appears rather than at the end of term, and tell the family what has been noticed, so a drift is interrupted early.
roleSupports.frequency: reviewed weekly, acted on in the same week
roleSupports.intensity: Weekly pattern check with a defined follow-up action

roleSupports.action: Restorative follow-up after conflict
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should hold a restorative conversation with {preferredName} after any conflict, once {preferredName} is regulated and as part of a planned return to the setting, covering what happened, who was affected and what will be done differently, so the return to class is planned rather than raw.
roleSupports.frequency: after each incident, before returning to the setting
roleSupports.intensity: Individual conversation with a plan for the return and any repair
evidence: repeat conflicts of the same kind

roleSupports.action: Be the consistent named adult
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should be {preferredName}'s consistent named adult across the year, known to {preferredName} and the family, with a named backup for absences, so there is always someone who knows the whole picture.
roleSupports.frequency: across the whole year, with a named backup
roleSupports.intensity: One consistent relationship, handed over only with a full briefing
evidence: who the student goes to when something is wrong

roleSupports.action: Plan the transition in
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should plan {preferredName}'s transition into the school or the next year level with orientation visits at quiet times, photos of the key places and adults, and a first-day plan, so the first day is familiar rather than new.
roleSupports.frequency: across the term before the transition
roleSupports.intensity: Several planned visits plus written and visual information for the student and family
evidence: student and family report of the first weeks

roleSupports.action: Hand the plan to the receiving staff before day one
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should pass {preferredName}'s plan and current adjustments to the receiving teachers or school, with consent, before the first day rather than after it, and confirm they have been read, so support starts on day one.
roleSupports.frequency: before the first day of the new setting or year
roleSupports.intensity: Documented handover with confirmation of receipt
evidence: adjustments in place in the first week

roleSupports.action: Plan the post-school pathway with the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should plan {preferredName}'s post-school pathway with {preferredName} and the family from the senior years onward, including the adjustments needed for work experience, further study or employment, so the pathway is built early and led by the student.
roleSupports.frequency: at least twice a year through the senior years
roleSupports.intensity: Student-led planning meetings with documented actions
evidence: student's stated goals and how they change

roleSupports.action: Manage mid-year changes of class or subject
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should manage any mid-year change of class, subject or teacher for {preferredName} as a planned transition, briefing the new staff and preparing {preferredName} beforehand, so a change of timetable does not undo settled routines.
roleSupports.frequency: before each mid-year change
roleSupports.intensity: Advance briefing of staff plus preparation with the student

roleSupports.action: Planned weekly check-in
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should hold a planned check-in with {preferredName} at an agreed time each week, in a consistent place with the same adult, so early signs of distress are noticed and acted on before they escalate.
roleSupports.frequency: once a week at an agreed time
roleSupports.intensity: Short individual conversation with the same adult each time
evidence: early signs noticed and what was done
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Coordinate a graduated return after absence
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should coordinate a written return-to-school plan for {preferredName} after any extended absence, setting out which classes are returned to first, who meets them at the gate and how the plan builds back to a full timetable, so returning is a supported process rather than a single hard day.
roleSupports.frequency: after any absence beyond the agreed threshold, reviewed weekly
roleSupports.intensity: Written plan, named adult on arrival, weekly review of the build-back
evidence: student and family report of the return
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Agree and teach a safe place and how to get there
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should agree a specific safe place with {preferredName}, document how it is accessed and who is notified, teach {preferredName} how to use it and brief the teaching team, so leaving a situation safely does not depend on negotiating it in the moment.
roleSupports.frequency: set up once, taught before it is needed, reviewed each term
roleSupports.intensity: Documented process, taught to the student, known by all their teachers
evidence: how often it is used and what triggered it
whether the student initiated it independently
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Co-design a 'what helps me' summary with the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should work with {preferredName} to write a short 'what helps me' summary in {preferredName}'s own words and, with their consent, share it with their teachers, so staff act on what the student says helps rather than on assumption.
roleSupports.frequency: written once and reviewed each semester with the student
roleSupports.intensity: Student-led drafting with adult scribing support, shared with consent
evidence: what the student names as helpful
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Hold the link with family and outside services
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should be the school's named contact with {preferredName}'s family and any outside service, with consent, passing on relevant information in both directions within an agreed timeframe, so the family tells the story once and school and service advice do not contradict each other.
roleSupports.frequency: contact at least fortnightly while support is active
roleSupports.intensity: Named single point of contact with documented information sharing
evidence: alignment between school and service advice
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Debrief staff after a significant incident
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should debrief the staff involved after any significant incident involving {preferredName}, within the same week, covering what happened, what worked and what will change, so the response improves and staff are supported.
roleSupports.frequency: within a week of any significant incident
roleSupports.intensity: Structured debrief with agreed changes recorded
evidence: repeat incidents of the same type
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Use the plan when setting classes and timetables
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should take {preferredName}'s plan into account when class lists, groupings and timetables are set, before the lists are finalised, so predictable difficulties are designed out rather than managed all year.
roleSupports.frequency: at each timetable or class list cycle
roleSupports.intensity: Plan consulted before decisions are locked in
evidence: placement decisions and how they worked out

roleSupports.action: Brief the year level team each term
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should brief the year level team on {preferredName}'s current adjustments at the start of each term, including what to do when things are not going well, so every teacher in the team is working from the same information.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each term
roleSupports.intensity: Team briefing with the written summary distributed
evidence: consistency of response reported across the team

roleSupports.action: Keep behaviour responses consistent with the plan
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should make sure responses to {preferredName}'s behaviour follow the agreed plan rather than the generic consequence, and check any referral against the plan before it proceeds, so the response accounts for the disability-related need.
roleSupports.frequency: whenever a behaviour response or referral is made
roleSupports.intensity: Plan checked before a consequence or referral is applied

roleSupports.action: Manage assessment load and clashes
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should monitor {preferredName}'s assessment load across subjects and adjust due dates where several fall in the same week, in line with the plan, so the workload is manageable without lowering what is expected.
roleSupports.frequency: at each assessment cycle
roleSupports.intensity: Cross-subject check with due dates adjusted where they clash
evidence: weeks where the load was adjusted

roleSupports.action: Coordinate ES staff deployment on the day
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should coordinate the deployment of ES and support staff for {preferredName} each day, matching staff to classes and activities in the plan, adjusting for absences and keeping a record of what was provided, so support is reliable rather than dependent on who is available.
roleSupports.frequency: at the start of each day, adjusted as the day unfolds
roleSupports.intensity: Daily coordination with a written record of deployment
evidence: lessons where the agreed support was not available and why

roleSupports.action: Triage on-the-day DI and student needs
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should triage on-the-day requests for DI related support for {preferredName} — new concerns, escalations and changes in presentation — deciding what can be handled immediately, what needs the DI leader and what needs the wellbeing or behaviour lead, so urgent needs are addressed quickly and nothing is missed.
roleSupports.frequency: as needs arise each day, with unresolved matters handed to the DI leader the same day
roleSupports.intensity: Single point of triage with a clear escalation path
actLabels: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

roleSupports.action: Brief and debrief ES staff around the student
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should brief ES staff working with {preferredName} at the start of the day on what is planned and debrief them at the end, passing on relevant teacher feedback and student voice, so support stays consistent and improvements are shared rather than isolated.
roleSupports.frequency: brief daily and debrief daily or at the end of the shift
roleSupports.intensity: Short structured handover with the plan as the reference

roleSupports.action: Keep DI admin and records current on the day
roleSupports.wording: The {role} should keep {preferredName}'s DI related admin current on the day — attendance at support, changes to deployment, notes from triage and handover — and pass a summary to the DI leader weekly, so the formal record reflects what actually happened.
roleSupports.frequency: daily notes, summarised weekly
roleSupports.intensity: Contemporaneous notes held in one place with a weekly summary
evidence: weekly summaries passed to the DI leader
